source.title: Regenerative Adaptation to Electrochemical Perturbation in Planaria: A Molecular Analysis of Physiological Plasticity.
source.location: Figure 1Ab; Results section 'When Exposed to BaCl2, Planaria Heads Rapidly Degenerate' (text)

intervention.description: Whole worms placed in 1 mM barium chloride solution (water-based) with no co-treatment.

readout.method: visual scoring of anterior head tissue in whole worms

notes: Text and Figure 1 legend: 83% of worms showed head degeneration, SD = 12% across all BaCl2 treatments. Figure legend says N > 50 per replicate, three replicates, so exact n is not stated (n_total null). Only the degenerate percentage is given; the remainder is not recorded. Family is planaria_screen (morphology endpoint) as the best fit; the paper scores head degeneration, not end-of-regeneration axis identity.

source.title: Regenerative Adaptation to Electrochemical Perturbation in Planaria: A Molecular Analysis of Physiological Plasticity.
source.location: Figure 1Bc; Results section 'Acquired Resistance to BaCl2 Is Lost after 30 Days in Water' (text)

intervention.timing: second exposure after 30 days in plain water (following earlier BaCl2 adaptation)
intervention.description: Worms previously exposed to 1 mM BaCl2 and regenerated heads, then kept in water for 30 days, then exposed again to 1 mM BaCl2 for 24 h.

readout.method: visual scoring of anterior head tissue in whole worms

notes: Text states 'All worms displayed characteristic degeneration' after the second BaCl2 round; read as 100%. No n stated, so n_total null. The day-30 water interval is stated; the exact start hour is not applicable.

readout.method: visual scoring of anterior head tissue in whole worms

notes: Text: 98% of heads fully degenerated by 24 h. Text also says 62% of worms died within 48 h with BaCl2 plus AMTB; that death count is recorded as dead_count but its timepoint (48 h) differs from the outcome timepoint (24 h). The two figures may refer to different worm groups and are not combined. No n stated.
